clue.text: Upper Circle

parts.note: the theatre's Upper Circle is a high gallery of seats, but read literally it is a ring floating above, as over a saint's head

explanation.surface: A theatre-goer names the seating tier they have booked.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make it look like a theatre balcony; read plainly it is a circle that sits up above something.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of light painted above a saint's head is literally a circle placed on high.

clue.text: Sacks those that take money

definitions.meaning: to sack is to dismiss, especially an officer from the forces in disgrace
people at tills or bank counters who receive payments

explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to dismiss from service; cashiers are also counter clerks handling payments.

clue.text: Start to wake up in prison

explanation.surface: Someone begins to come round from sleep inside a jail cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper begins to move as they wake, and the same short word is old slang for jail.

clue.text: Safety first with missile launched from submarine grating

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Safety is wanted here

parts.note: Trident is the ballistic missile fired from Royal Navy and US Navy submarines

explanation.surface: A naval briefing stresses safety before a submarine fires its missile through a grating.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating noise is harsh and shrill, which is exactly what a loud, jarring voice is.

clue.text: Nod when told to go?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
someone sent away has been told to go

explanation.surface: Someone gives a nod when they are ordered to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'when told to go' is not a homophone hint but two plain pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod of the head signals agreement or approval.

clue.text: Criminal macho characteristic

parts.note: macho describes something typically masculine
a factor is a contributing feature or element

explanation.surface: Is aggressive manliness the trait that marks out a criminal?
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer or lawbreaker is a criminal; the word is a noun in both senses.

clue.text: Formidable woman appears to be tedious

definitions.meaning: a fierce, intimidating woman, as in an old battleaxe
split as two words, to ... is to seem to go on wearisomely

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman turns out to be a bore.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, domineering woman is called a fire-breathing monster, and split in two the word means to continue wearisomely.

clue.text: Get out of this!

parts.note: read as an instruction, it points to a way out, such as the sign over a door

explanation.surface: An angry order for someone to leave the room.
explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a shouted dismissal, but 'this' is the thing you leave by: a door marked as the way out.
explanation.definitionFit: A door marked for leaving is the way you get out of a building.

clue.text: Separate craft in which father's conveyed

indicators.note: the word for craft is the vessel that the father goes inside
carried inside, so the father is held within the craft

parts.note: art means skill or craft
pa is a familiar word for father; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A father is carried aboard a separate vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat, which suits 'conveyed', but it means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept at a distance from one another are separate, the adverb form of being split up.

clue.text: Willing female

parts.note: not an eager woman but a woman making a will

explanation.surface: It sounds like a description of an obliging woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' means drawing up a will, not keen.
explanation.definitionFit: This legal term names a woman who has made a will, the feminine of testator.

clue.text: Mother wisely included it — or else!

indicators.note: the letters run on inside the words Mother wisely, so the answer is held within them

explanation.surface: A mother wisely threatens a child: do it, or else!
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean 'if not', the warning of a consequence.

clue.text: Oarsmen include a soldier in the overturned boat

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so the assembled letters are read backwards
the soldier goes inside the word the

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Rowers take a soldier aboard and their boat capsizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' makes THGIE, and 'overturned boat' reads it backwards; the boat and its crew share the answer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing crew of that many oarsmen is named for its number, and the boat shares the name.

clue.text: Quickest way home for some workers

definitions.text: Quickest way home for some workers

parts.words: Quickest way home for some workers
parts.note: the workers are worker bees, flying straight back to the hive

explanation.surface: It reads like a commuter's tip for the fastest route home.
explanation.walkthrough: The workers are worker bees, not office staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight route between two points, said to be the line a bee flies back to its hive.

clue.text: Feature of barley used to make bread

indicators.note: the letters of bread are used to make something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A baker notes a feature of barley grain that goes into bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Barley ears carry long bristles called awns, collectively known by the same word as a man's whiskers.

clue.text: Foreign parts?

parts.note: not overseas lands but foreign bodies, contaminating parts of a substance

explanation.surface: It looks like a phrase for travelling abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' here means alien matter in something, not abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Contaminants are foreign matter mixed into a substance that should be pure.

clue.text: One under instruction to make a stand about wet weather

indicators.note: the stand goes round the wet weather, holding it within

parts.note: a tee is the small stand a golf ball rests on
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A learner is told to put up a shelter against the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A person being taught or apprenticed is someone under instruction.

clue.text: Peg-legged supporter of the school board

definitions.text: Peg-legged supporter of the school board

parts.words: Peg-legged supporter of the school board
parts.note: not a one-legged governor but a stand with pegged legs holding up a blackboard

explanation.surface: It suggests a one-legged backer of the board of school governors.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'school board' is a blackboard, and 'peg-legged' describes the stand's adjustable legs with pegs.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden stand on legs, with pegs to set the height, holds a blackboard or a painter's canvas.

clue.text: He told tales for soap set around English capital

indicators.note: the rearranged soap goes round the English letter
the letters of soap are set into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told stories in exchange for soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges SOAP to ASOP, and 'around' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist is the classic teller of moral animal stories.

clue.text: Hal stopped with him

indicators.note: the name Hal joined with this man's name makes a word for stopped, so taking Hal away leaves him

parts.note: halted means stopped
taken as written, the start of the word for stopped

explanation.surface: Hal and a companion came to a standstill together.
explanation.walkthrough: Put Hal with the answer and you get HALTED (stopped); 'him' is just a man, here a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A short male first name stands for a man, the 'him' of the clue.

clue.text: Intended to put one's name in a legal document

indicators.note: the signing goes inside the legal document

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
to sign is to put one's name to something

explanation.surface: Someone meant to sign a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Something planned or done on purpose was intended; both are past participles.

clue.text: VAT, say, for nails

indicators.note: say marks VAT as an example and also signals that the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: value added tax, a kind of tax

explanation.surface: A DIY shopper wonders whether the price of nails includes VAT.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, the British sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sharp nails with broad heads, as used for carpets, are a type of nail.

clue.text: The settlement is due to him

definitions.text: The settlement is due to him

parts.words: The settlement is due to him
parts.note: settlement means payment of a debt, owed to the lender

explanation.surface: It sounds as if one man brought about a colony or a peace deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlement' is the settling of a bill, and 'due to' means owed to, not caused by.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender is the person a debt is owed to, so payment is owed to them.

clue.text: Wanted to be a schoolmaster, in fact

indicators.note: the schoolmaster goes inside the fact

parts.note: a deed is a fact, as in 'in deed' for in fact
pupils address a schoolmaster as sir

explanation.surface: Someone longed to become a schoolmaster, in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Something longed for was wanted; both are past forms of the verb.

clue.text: It's bound to go on foot

definitions.text: It's bound to go on foot

parts.words: It's bound to go on foot
parts.note: not certain to walk, but strapped onto a foot

explanation.surface: It reads as something certain to travel on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' means tied with straps, not destined.
explanation.definitionFit: Open shoes are held on by straps tied round the foot.

clue.text: Obtuse humour of a stupid person

parts.note: obtuse means slow-witted, dim
wit is humour

explanation.surface: Slow humour is the mark of a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard or fool is a stupid person.

clue.text: A ruler's confused in a dream world

definitions.note: describing something bizarre and dreamlike, as an adjective

indicators.note: the letters of a ruler's are mixed up

explanation.surface: A monarch is muddled and living in a fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrealist painters depicted bizarre, dreamlike scenes, so the word describes the strangeness of dreams.

clue.text: French painter changes, not me

indicators.note: the letters of not me change into a new order

explanation.surface: A French artist declares he alters everything except himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude of that name was the French Impressionist who painted water lilies.

clue.text: Wise men have a month in Paris about the end of spring

indicators.note: the French month goes round the final letter

parts.note: mai is French for May

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word spring is taken

explanation.surface: Sages spend a month in Paris as spring ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The three wise men who visited the infant Jesus are known by this Persian-derived plural.

clue.text: Made to look great!

parts.note: not flattered but made to look bigger, as through a lens

explanation.surface: A compliment after a makeover: you look wonderful!
explanation.definitionFit: A lens enlarges what you see, making an object appear larger than it is.

clue.text: Unemployed paid less at the centre

indicators.note: the answer sits at the centre of the words paid less, held inside them

explanation.surface: Jobless people are paid less, the clue suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no work is out of a job, without employment.

clue.text: Might it turn the tide for those overweight?

definitions.text: Might it turn the tide for those overweight?

indicators.note: turn tells the solver to turn the letters of tide around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Could a weight-loss regime reverse the trend for the overweight?
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges TIDE, and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimming eating plan is what an overweight person adopts to change course.

clue.text: Even a prig could be a passer-on of gossip

indicators.note: the letters of even a prig could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Even a prudish person might spread gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing news 'on the grapevine' means by rumour, so the informal network itself carries gossip.

clue.text: Nothing to to do at this end

definitions.text: Nothing to to do at this end

parts.words: Nothing to to do at this end
parts.note: having nothing to do is being 'at a ... end', and this word fills that idiom

explanation.surface: A worker complains that their side of the operation has nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'at a loose end' means idle; the doubled 'to' is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being idle with nothing to occupy you is being at an untied end.
